The goal is to minimize the total transportation cost while ensuring that all cities receive the resources they need, without exceeding the capacity of the transportation links or the storage capacity of the cities.

The maximum capacity for transporting resources from City 0 to City 1 is 7 units, to City 2 is 9 units, to City 3 is 7 units, to City 4 is 8 units, to City 5 is 9 units, to City 6 is 7 units, and to City 7 is 7 units. import pyomo.environ as pyo

DATA = {
    "nodes": [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7],
    # net demand: positive = demand, negative = supply, 0 = balanced
    "net_demand": {0: 2, 1: 0, 2: -1, 3: 2, 4: -2, 5: 0, 6: 1, 7: -2},
    "cost": {
        (0, 1): 1, (0, 2): 1, (0, 3): 1, (0, 4): 1, (0, 5): 3, (0, 6): 3, (0, 7): 3,
        (1, 0): 1, (1, 2): 2, (1, 3): 2, (1, 4): 2, (1, 5): 3, (1, 6): 2, (1, 7): 1,

    },
    "link_capacity": {
        (0, 1): 7, (0, 2): 9, (0, 3): 7, (0, 4): 8, (0, 5): 9, (0, 6): 7, (0, 7): 7,
        (1, 0): 8, (1, 2): 8, (1, 3): 8, (1, 4): 7, (1, 5): 9, (1, 6): 8, (1, 7): 9,
        (2, 0): 7, (2, 1): 9, (2, 3): 9, (2, 4): 7, (2, 5): 9, (2, 6): 8, (2, 7): 9,
        (3, 0): 8, (3, 1): 8, (3, 2): 9, (3, 4): 7, (3, 5): 9, (3, 6): 7, (3, 7): 8,
        (4, 0): 7, (4, 1): 7, (4, 2): 7, (4, 3): 9, (4, 5): 8, (4, 6): 7, (4, 7): 7,
        (5, 0): 9, (5, 1): 9, (5, 2): 9, (5, 3): 9, (5, 4): 7, (5, 6): 7, (5, 7): 7,
        (6, 0): 8, (6, 1): 9, (6, 2): 7, (6, 3): 9, (6, 4): 9, (6, 5): 7, (6, 7): 9,
        (7, 0): 9, (7, 1): 7, (7, 2): 8, (7, 3): 8, (7, 4): 8, (7, 5): 9, (7, 6): 8,
    },
    "storage_capacity": {0: 16, 1: 16, 2: 18, 3: 12, 4: 14, 5: 16, 6: 12, 7: 14},
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA

    nodes = list(d["nodes"])
    arcs = list(d["cost"].keys())

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.N = pyo.Set(initialize=nodes, ordered=True)
    model.A = pyo.Set(dimen=2, initialize=arcs, ordered=True)

    # Flow on each directed link, bounded by link capacity, non-negative.
    model.x = pyo.Var(
        model.A,
        domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals,
        bounds=lambda mm, i, j: (0, d["link_capacity"][(i, j)]),
    )

    def obj_rule(mm):
        return sum(d["cost"][(i, j)] * mm.x[i, j] for (i, j) in mm.A)

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # Link capacity: flow on a link cannot exceed its stated capacity.
    def link_cap_rule(mm, i, j):
        return mm.x[i, j] <= d["link_capacity"][(i, j)]

    model.link_capacity = pyo.Constraint(model.A, rule=link_cap_rule)

    # Inbound / outbound flow helpers expressed as constraints.
    def inbound_expr(mm, n):
        return sum(mm.x[i, n] for (i, j) in mm.A if j == n)

    def outbound_expr(mm, n):
        return sum(mm.x[n, j] for (i, j) in mm.A if i == n)

    # Net balance: outbound - inbound = net demand for each city.
    def balance_rule(mm, n):
        return outbound_expr(mm, n) - inbound_expr(mm, n) == d["net_demand"][n]

    model.balance = pyo.Constraint(model.N, rule=balance_rule)

    # Explicit demand satisfaction: a demand city must receive at least its demand.
    model.D = pyo.Set(initialize=[n for n in nodes if d["net_demand"][n] > 0], ordered=True)

    def demand_satisfaction_rule(mm, n):
        return inbound_expr(mm, n) >= d["net_demand"][n]

    model.demand_satisfaction = pyo.Constraint(model.D, rule=demand_satisfaction_rule)

    # Supply availability: a supply city cannot ship out more than its supply.
    model.S = pyo.Set(initialize=[n for n in nodes if d["net_demand"][n] < 0], ordered=True)

    def supply_limit_rule(mm, n):
        return outbound_expr(mm, n) <= -d["net_demand"][n]

    model.supply_limit = pyo.Constraint(model.S, rule=supply_limit_rule)

    # Storage capacity: inbound flow to a city cannot exceed its storage capacity.
    def storage_rule(mm, n):
        return inbound_expr(mm, n) <= d["storage_capacity"][n]

    model.storage = pyo.Constraint(model.N, rule=storage_rule)

    return model
